headline: Crude bomb explodes in front of Supreme Court
summary: The blast occurred shortly after the International Crimes Tribunal-2 sentenced seven Awami League leaders to death.
details: A crude bomb exploded in front of the Supreme Court in Dhaka this afternoon around 1:15 pm.
The incident took place approximately one hour after the International Crimes Tribunal-2 delivered a significant verdict.
The tribunal had sentenced Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others to death in a crimes against humanity case.
The other convicts include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash.
Additionally, Moinul Hossain Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan were among those sentenced to death.
Shahbagh Police Station Inspector (Operations) Mainul Islam confirmed the blast and stated that police are now working to identify the perpetrators.
caption:
A crude bomb blast rocks the Supreme Court area in Dhaka.

The other convicts include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash.

Additionally, Moinul Hossain Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan were among those sentenced to death.

Shahbagh Police Station Inspector (Operations) Mainul Islam confirmed the blast and stated that police are now working to identify the perpetrators.

headline_marked: Extradition of [[Hasina and Quader needed to ease ties]] with India: Zahed
headline: Extradition of Hasina and Quader needed to ease ties with India: Zahed
summary: Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman states that handing over fugitive convicts including Sheikh Hasina and Obaidul Quader is a key condition for improving relations with India.
details: Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the return of fugitive and convicted persons, including Sheikh Hasina and Obaidul Quader, is an important condition for easing relations between Bangladesh and India.
During a press briefing at the Secretariat, the adviser mentioned that this position was clearly raised during a courtesy meeting with the Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh.
Zahed Ur Rahman emphasized that the Indian government should consider this matter seriously to strengthen working engagement with Bangladesh.
The adviser noted that Sheikh Hasina's brutality was not limited to July alone but continued for years, and that several people were involved in these acts.
He added that fugitive accused persons making statements on social media from abroad are severely hurting the sentiments of the people of Bangladesh.
The government's top priority is ensuring justice for crimes committed under the Awami league rule, with the adviser stating there will be no compromise on justice.
Regarding local government elections, Zahed said the Election Commission and the government will jointly decide on the timing and process, which will be fully participatory and without party symbols.
He also confirmed that 10,000 workers are being sent to Malaysia free of cost and mentioned a policy is being formulated to regulate battery-run auto-rickshaws instead of stopping them altogether.
caption:
Handing over Sheikh Hasina and Obaidul Quader is a 'very important condition' for easing ties with India, says Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman.

Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the return of fugitive and convicted persons, including Sheikh Hasina and Obaidul Quader, is an important condition for easing relations between Bangladesh and India.

During a press briefing at the Secretariat, the adviser mentioned that this position was clearly raised during a courtesy meeting with the Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh.

Zahed Ur Rahman emphasized that the Indian government should consider this matter seriously to strengthen working engagement with Bangladesh.

The adviser noted that Sheikh Hasina's brutality was not limited to July alone but continued for years, and that several people were involved in these acts.

He added that fugitive accused persons making statements on social media from abroad are severely hurting the sentiments of the people of Bangladesh.

The government's top priority is ensuring justice for crimes committed under the Awami league rule, with the adviser stating there will be no compromise on justice.

Regarding local government elections, Zahed said the Election Commission and the government will jointly decide on the timing and process, which will be fully participatory and without party symbols.

He also confirmed that 10,000 workers are being sent to Malaysia free of cost and mentioned a policy is being formulated to regulate battery-run auto-rickshaws instead of stopping them altogether.
